Current industrial strategies heavily emphasize macroeconomic recovery and resource optimization. Recent initiatives highlight South Africa's potential to reestablish itself as a major value-adding minerals player, emphasizing industrial strategies rather than specific IT contract data [80] . Furthermore, regional administrative efforts reflect a broader focus on operational compliance and labor dynamics rather than technology procurement. For instance, there is an ongoing nationwide audit in southern Africa tied to contract mining value capture initiatives, with a December 2026 deadline, but it provides no insights on IT contract durations and offers only a regional context [81] . Analyses of global mining costs, inflationary pressures, and supply chain adjustments focus on macroeconomic factors rather than the specifics of IT expenditures or procurement in South Africa [83] . Additionally, major industry events and platforms designed to foster sector growth tend to prioritize broad investment themes. The thematic priorities for the 2026 Investing in Mining Indaba include showcasing mineral resources and attracting investors, but they do not delve into IT spending or contract specifics [22][Investing in 22 will mark a defining ... - Facebook] .
